taxonomic_note: Accepted at species rank. A later illegitimate use of the name by L.f. is not treated as a separate learner taxon.
look_here_first: RED FLOWERS ARE NOT THE ID. Start with the LEAVES: scarlet sage has many broad triangular-to-ovate SIMPLE leaves on prominent petioles up an upright, branching stem, not a cedar-sage basal rosette nor big-red-sage's large thick smooth basal leaves. Check the interrupted flower spike and calyces next; wild flowers are often red but cultivated selections can also be pink/white.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Opposite broad triangular to ovate-deltoid serrate leaves on conspicuous petioles, 4-angled stems, repeated flower verticils, persistent ribbed calyx, and long bilabiate corolla.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual to short-lived perennial/subshrub tendency; usually branched, often 0.5–1 m tall.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite decussate, simple, petiolate; blades triangular or ovate to deltoid with serrate margins.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Interrupted series of verticils/cymes along a terminal axis.
morphology_keys.calyx: Persistent, ribbed and enlarging around developing nutlets.
morphology_keys.floral_detail: Long bilateral corolla; typically red in local material but color is secondary to leaf and inflorescence structure.
morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual or short-lived perennial depending on frost and site, herbaceous branched upper stems; an open, weedlike shoot is supportive but not sole proof.
morphology_keys.leaf_diagnostic: Simple (one undivided blade), opposite broad ovate/deltoid, petiolate with serrate edges; no lateral leaflets as on some cedar sage leaves.
morphology_keys.flower_arrangement: Red tubular two-lipped corollas in separate spaced flowering whorls on branched/terminal upright spikes; persistent calyces remain after petals fall.
morphology_keys.compare_roemeriana: Cedar sage is a taprooted perennial with conspicuous basal rosette and leaves sometimes 1–3-foliolate on long petioles. Its calyx is ~11 mm (UT), and flower spikes usually arise from a woodland leaf rosette.
morphology_keys.compare_pentstemonoides: Big red sage has thick, smooth, large basal rosette leaves (to ~12 cm) and flowers about 4 cm, on tall stalks (to ~1.5 m), usually seep-fed limestone ravines; FWS source.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Cedar sage may also be red but has a low shaded-juniper habitat and different leaf architecture. Azure sage has narrow linear leaves and a much taller open flowering axis.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: SCARLET = stem leaves, SIMPLE blades. CEDAR = woodland ROSETTE, sometimes leaflets. BIG RED = BIG thick rosette, BIG tubular flowers.
